--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [DataScan.from_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Restore a DataScan from a JSON string. twitter-card: title: >- [DataScan.from_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Restore a DataScan from a JSON string. title: >- [DataScan.from_json()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Restore a DataScan from a JSON string. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Restore a `DataScan` from a JSON string. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/datascan.py#L994-L1049){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature DataScan.from_json(json_string) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The JSON string is the one produced by [`to_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.to_json`). It's the counterpart to that method for profiles stored as text, such as in a database column or an API response. To read a JSON file, use [`load_from_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.load_from_json`). As with [`from_dict()`](`pointblank.DataScan.from_dict`), the restored scan has the statistics but not the data. Values that were written as strings in the JSON (such as dates) stay strings. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [json_string]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A JSON string as produced by [`to_json()`](`pointblank.DataScan.to_json`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataScan]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A restored `DataScan` instance. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Suppose the profile of the `small_table` dataset was stored as JSON text some time ago. ::: {#6b090548 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl small_table = pb.load_dataset(dataset="small_table", tbl_type="polars") stored_json = pb.DataScan(small_table, tbl_name="small_table").to_json() ``` ::: Restoring it gives a `DataScan` that can be queried like the original one: ::: {#898129f7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} restored = pb.DataScan.from_json(stored_json) restored.summary_data.select("colname", "n_missing", "n_unique") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (8, 3)
colnamen_missingn_unique
stri64i64
"date_time"012
"date"011
"a"07
"b"012
"c"27
"d"012
"e"02
"f"03
``` ::: ::: The table name, row count, and every column's statistics come from the JSON, so the original table isn't needed to answer questions about it later.
